title: Stuck with 2d top down map building
author: Romellija
selftext:
Hi all

I'm just wondering if anyone has any good workflow or advice on building 2d top down maps that give the illusion of 3d. I've tried various ways but nothing seems to look good.

For example, Baking the majority of the map in an image looks too flat.

Doing a terrain image and then putting props/assets on top never seem to match up. 

Just looking for any advice you have on this.

comments.author: zenmatrix83
comments.body: you want 2.5d try to look for workflows relating to that, sometimes thats custom sprites, sometimes that is static 3d models with a static camera

replies.author: Romellija
replies.body:
I haven't tried the 3d models with astatic camera actually.

 I've tried creating all sorts of sprites for a 3d effect but hasn't really worked properly yet. I also find the terrain difficult as it's difficult to get assets that tile correctly and doing s terrain image usually looks too AI e.g overdetailed. 

I'll try the 3d models route tho tha k you for the response

comments.author: Anarye
comments.body:
Similar issues. Using hexagons for my map and using building images as overlays on top of biome tiles that I created.

Problem im having is that AI cant properly size nor build the assets to fit naturally into the tiles. 

The look im trying to accomplish is an isometric view with a 85 degree down angle. So not quite top down, but close.

comments.author: loopywolf
comments.body: I can't help but I get it.  I just went through this for my game and the art style is CRITICAL..  I think I went through 4 iterations before I settled on what I wanted

comments.author: Ok-Suspect-9855
comments.body: Generate the whole image with all items. Use mask models to select the items and cut them out and make new layer. Use another model to remove the layer that was cut from the image.

comments.author: deintag85
comments.body: Show us an example of what you got. Don’t know exactly what you want. Did you try shadows? They give a bit 3d feeling.
